headline: The Armed Forces of Burkina Faso have released footage showing artillery units conducting live-fire exercises using an almost entirely Chinese lineup of fire-support and strike systems. Equipment seen in the footage: • Batteries of 122 mm CS/SH1 self-propelled howitzers on Shaanxi 6×6 chassis, with a firing range of 22–27 km; • 120 mm PLL-05 self-propelled mortars mounted on the Type 92 variant of the WZ551 wheeled chassis, with a firing range of up to 13 km and a digital fire-control system; • SR-5 (PHL-11) Multiple Rocket Launcher (MRL) on heavy 8×8 chassis, equipped with guided 220 mm rockets with a range of up to 70 km. In the second part of the video, the Tianlong-30 (Sky Dragon 30) surface-to-air missile (SAM) system was publicly shown for the first time. Its delivery to Burkina Faso had not previously been reported. The footage shows a launcher and an IBIS-150 three-coordinate radar, capable of detecting targets at ranges of up to 130 km and tracking up to 144 targets. The primary missile is the SD-30, which uses combined guidance and has a reported engagement range of up to 30 km.

headline: The USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) docked at Laem Chabang, Thailand, earlier today, marking its first port visit where sailors will be afforded liberty ashore since departing Naval Base San Diego, California, on November 21, 2025. The carrier made a brief one day logistics stop in Guam on December 11 before departing the following day and continuing west. Lincoln arrived in the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations in the Middle East on January 26, 2026, where it supported combat operations against Iran for months before being relieved by the USS George Washington (CVN-73) approximately two weeks ago. The port visit in Thailand comes after one of the longest sustained operational periods for a U.S. aircraft carrier in recent years, giving the crew its first opportunity for a significant liberty port visit since leaving San Diego. Photo: Reuters
